credits: Alesis: the Quadraverb (1989) and its factory programs (software by Fast Forward Designs, hardware by Keith Barr and Alan Zak), which the build compiles from the owner's own ROM image; no Alesis program is in this repository
repeat98: the reverse engineering of the Quadraverb's DSP, the integer model and the compiled engine

presentation.label: 1989 DIGITAL REVERB
presentation.summary: 22 reverbs of the Alesis Quadraverb (1989), each its original factory program run step for step on FX2.
presentation.overview: Rooms, halls, chambers and plates from the Quadraverb's factory programs. Each is the original's 96-step DSP program, compiled to DSP code when you pick it and run at 44.1 kHz; its long delay lines live in the Octatrack's main memory. Not compared with a real Quadraverb.
highlights: 22 original reverb programs: rooms, halls, chambers, plates
Each program is the original's, step for step, with its own LFO sweeps
PROG picks the program by its number on the original; MIX 0 is exact dry
usage: Choose QUADRAVERB in FX2 SETUP: hold FUNC, press FX2, turn LEVEL to it and press YES, then press FX2 for the main page.
PROG (A) picks the program by its number on the original Quadraverb: 10-12 rooms, 13-16 halls, 17-19 plates, 20-22 chambers.

controls.name: PROG
controls.doc: the factory program, by its number on the original Quadraverb (10 SMALL ROOM by default)

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet: 0 is exact dry, 127 wet only

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base's program areas and stream channel (loader ABI 9, the package requires `programs`), so it is USB-only. They are in the base 0.8.3 draft, on development twins only so far.

FX2 only: each instance uses the first 15,870 words of its track's 16K-word FX2 buffer for its short delay lines, and keeps its long ones in the ColdFire's memory, which the base moves to and from the DSP every 16 samples.

One instance a DSP core at most: its two program areas take up to 2,336 of the about 4,700 words a core has for effect code, beside a Part's stock effects. The ColdFire's ring pool holds one plate, or two chambers, or a chamber and a room; a slot without room stays dry.

Each pick writes the program's code into one of two areas the base holds for the slot, so a pick is silent for a moment while the code and the new reverb's memory start; the other area keeps the program before.

Unlike the original: 44.1 kHz instead of about 42 kHz (reverb times, delays and sweeps about 5 % shorter and faster), a mono input from the average of left and right, 24-bit words in the DSP and 16 bits where a word crosses to the ColdFire. Not compared with a real Quadraverb.
The gated reverbs (3, 23-27) are not in this release: their gate needs a signal detector the original has in hardware.
Built from the owner's own Quadraverb 1.07 ROM image on the developer's computer: the build reads it, and nothing derived from it is in this repository.

storage.label: DSP program / state
storage.display: two areas of 919-1,168 words a slot / 132-word state
storage.conditions: Two program areas a slot on its core (program_words 1,168), the 25-word shell, the r7 block $00-$83, up to 15,870 words of the track's FX2 buffer in Y, and on the ColdFire 82,668 bytes of code and data plus a 136 KiB ring pool in bss. See TESTING.md.

processing.label: DSP cycles
processing.conditions: interlock_scan's stall model on step traces in dsp_host of the release form, all 22 programs, one instance, every place a tick can fall in a 16-sample block (engine/verify_area.py --cycles): the dearest, program 53, 341.6 in its dearest block and 353.1 while a pick fades it; declared 355 modeled. A model, not a measurement on a unit.

cpuPrice.conditions: Provisional, not measured: the stream's transfers (about 0.07 us a halfword, up to 352 in and 144 out a frame for the plates) and the ColdFire's copies run in the frame interrupt. To be measured on a unit with npm run device:price (TESTING.md).

tests.summary: Built on the developer's computer (27 Nov 2026), not run on a unit or heard. In dsp_host the release's shell and areas run all 22 programs bit-exact against the integer model with the stream as the ColdFire half sends it; the ColdFire half matches its model on the host. The development builds of programs 5, 40 and 56 were priced on an MKII.
gates: Worst-case cycles under parameter modulation and maximum load
Exact memory region and maximum-instance totals
Owner-reviewed real-hardware evidence with actual coverage and limitations

license.declaration: The module's own code and documentation are MIT (LICENSE). The Alesis Quadraverb programs are not in this repository: the build compiles them from the owner's own ROM image into gen/ (ignored by Git) and ~/.cache, and the packages built from them stay on the developer's computer until the owner allows their inclusion. No Elektron firmware, routines or tables are included.

otUi.setup: Emulator captures, not hardware ones. ot_emu built from the pinned upstream source (emulatorSha256), MKII panel, run by npm run device:emulator with --dsp on development twin 7520dee5 of the base 0.8.3 side branch (base/octatrack-program-areas 5ecfbd2f4; imageSha256 is its MAIN image). The package named here, built from the source revision named here with the owner's ROM on his computer, was installed with the session's try. This emulator runs no DSP passes, so nothing was heard and the pick shows only the pages; the frame guard's share was set to 100 % and the CPU allowance to 100 % first (guard:1000 cpu:100), as the emulator's CPU meter reads full. Each picture is the emulated LCD read by the development session's png step: 128x64 at integer scale 2 (256x128), two grey levels in an 8-bit greyscale PNG, not edited. Panel steps: T5; FUNC+FX2; LEVEL to QUADRAVERB; YES; FX2; then A and F turned.

access.location: Audio track FX2 SETUP: QUADRAVERB in the effect chooser.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 to open FX2 SETUP.
Turn LEVEL to QUADRAVERB and press YES.
Press FX2 for the main page: PROG on knob A, MIX on knob F.
